TestReadRepair::test_alter_rf_and_run_re.description: 3 nodes (dc1: rack1=2, rack2=1), NTS RF=1 keyspace, insert row (1,1,1), flush on the replica found via nodetool getendpoints, check CL ONE read from every coordinator returns full row. ALTER RF to 2 (rack list if RF is auto-expanded) without repair, then SELECT a single column at CL ALL from a non-initial replica to trigger read repair; asserts the result has only the column, then CL ONE reads from every node must return the full row. Guards CASSANDRA-10655 (column-filtered data responses causing empty values in repair mutations), i.e. read repair must repair whole row even for partial-column selects.

origin.summary: Cassandra-dtest commit 'Add read repair test for CASSANDRA-10655' (Sam Tunnicliffe), imported via scylla-dtest PR #52 'Merge upstream'; not Scylla-specific.

TestReadRepair::test_alter_rf_and_run_re.relevance: Read repair on digest mismatch is live in scylla (service/storage_proxy.cc 'digest mismatch, starting read repair', read_repair_write_attempts). But with tablets (next-dtest-tablets job) ALTER KEYSPACE RF increase triggers tablet rebuild/streaming to the new replica before the ALTER completes (test/cluster/test_tablets.py::test_singledc_alter_tablets_rf), so the new replica already has the full row and read repair is not exercised; only meaningful in vnodes mode. Only runs in next-* gating jobs (100% pass, 32 runs, ~15s).

duplicates.note: Read repair at CL ALL with replica missing data, verifies rows on both nodes afterwards; no partial-column select / RF change.
Missing writes on one replica (injection), CL ALL read triggers read repair (trace check).

TestReadRepair::test_alter_rf_and_run_re.reason: Partial overlap with test/cluster/test_read_repair.py; the specific angle (partial-column select repairs whole row, CASSANDRA-10655) is not covered there, but under tablets the ALTER RF rebuild streams data so read repair is never exercised — evidence for vnodes-only value is thin. Note: unused var num_nodes (read_repair_test.py:37); identify_initial_placement ignores its keyspace/table/key args and hardcodes 'getendpoints alter_rf_test t1 1' (read_repair_test.py:91-93); CL ALL assertion only checks the selected column.

TestReadRepair::test_range_slice_query_w.description: 3 nodes, NTS RF=2, insert 2499 rows, flush, restart cluster, delete keys 1..999, flush node1, then traced 'SELECT * LIMIT 100' at LOCAL_QUORUM. Asserts no trace event contains 'Appending to commitlog', 'Adding to cf memtable' or 'Acquiring switchLock read lock', i.e. range scans over tombstones must not trigger unnecessary read-repair writes (CASSANDRA-8989 / CASSANDRA-9502).

TestReadRepair::test_range_slice_query_w.relevance: The three asserted strings are Cassandra trace messages; none exist anywhere in scylla source (grep of *.cc/*.hh at 814c05a00f finds no 'Appending to commitlog', 'Adding to ... memtable', 'switchLock'). Scylla's read-repair trace events are e.g. 'digest mismatch, starting read repair' and 'Creating write handler for read repair token' (service/storage_proxy.cc:3921). So the assertions can never fail on scylla.
